title: Dedline
summary: A Flutter app that keeps subscriptions, renewals and other recurring commitments from catching you off guard — built on a Supabase backend with an AI step that pulls subscription details out of documents.

caseStudy.overview: Dedline began as a local-only deadline tracker and is being rebuilt into a subscription tracker: what you pay for, when it renews, and a reminder early enough to cancel or budget for it.
caseStudy.problem: Renewal dates rarely repeat often enough to stay in your head. They sit in an email from eight months ago, and the first reminder is the charge itself. General to-do apps treat them like any other task, with no amount, billing cycle or provider attached.
contribution: Set the V1 scope: Android first, single-user accounts, and a currency-agnostic schema with NGN as the default.
Structured the app by feature (auth, subscriptions, categories, onboarding, settings, AI extraction), each split into data, domain and presentation layers.
Moved persistence from an on-device Drift/SQLite database to Supabase in stages, keeping the app working at each step.
constraints: Android-only first release, to keep the scope small enough to ship.
New personal Google Play accounts must run a 14-day closed test with at least 12 testers before production — a release-date constraint unrelated to engineering speed.
API keys for the AI step can't ship inside the app.
caseStudy.approach: Evolve the existing codebase rather than start over. Its routing, theming, calendar view and notification scheduling were sound, so the work went into the data model and backend: subscription entities, Supabase auth, Postgres tables behind row-level security, file storage, and a server-side extraction function.

decisions.title: Rebuild on the existing app, not from scratch
decisions.body: The existing architecture already handled navigation, theming and reminders well. Keeping it meant the effort went into what was missing — a real backend and a subscription data model.

decisions.title: Retire the local database completely
decisions.body: Once subscriptions lived in Supabase, the Drift/SQLite layer was removed rather than kept in sync. The only local state left is reminder notification IDs, in shared_preferences.

decisions.title: Run AI extraction in an Edge Function
decisions.body: Pulling subscription details out of an uploaded document happens in a Supabase Edge Function, so model credentials stay server-side and the client only calls an RPC.

decisions.title: Security in the database, not just the client
decisions.body: Row-level security policies are part of the schema migrations, so each user can only reach their own rows no matter which client makes the request.
